question.problem:
$$ \{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=-2{x}_{1}(t)+9{x}_{2}(t)-20 \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)={x}_{2}(t)-2,\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}] $$ Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a transformed system with the solution $$ {X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}=\frac{2}{s+2}+\frac{3}{s-1}-\frac{1}{s},\,{X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}=\frac{1}{s-1}+\frac{2}{s}. $$ Find the solution to the original initial value problem.
$x(t)=\,\,$ {{field-1}}
{{field-2}}
question.worked_solution:
To find ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t)$ satisfying the original initial value problem, we apply the inverse Laplace transform to ${X}_{1}(s)$ and ${X}_{2}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & ={L}^{-1}\{{X}_{1}(s)\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{2}{s+2}+\frac{3}{s-1}-\frac{1}{s}\} \\  & =2\,{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s+2}\}+3\,{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-1}\}-{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s}\} \\  & =2{e}^{-2\cdot t}+3{e}^{1\cdot t}-1 \\  & =3{e}^{t}-1+2{e}^{-2t} \\ {x}_{2}(t) & ={L}^{-1}\{{X}_{2}(s)\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-1}+\frac{2}{s}\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-1}\}+2\,{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s}\} \\  & ={e}^{1\cdot t}+2 \\  & ={e}^{t}+2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the solution to the initial value problem:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3{e}^{t}-1+2{e}^{-2t} \\ {e}^{t}+2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
